# Native USB4 Completion Plan — handmade ASM2464PD firmware

Scope: take the from-scratch flat-bank0 SDCC image from its current stopping point (PD contract + VDM + Enter_USB accepted; `[Connect_U4]` reached; `int1` USB4 demux wired in `usb4.h` as observe-and-ack only; **E302 never trains because the device never asserts the sideband**) to a GPU in `lspci`. Source files: `/home/batman/asm2464pd-firmware/handmade/src/{pd.h,vdm.h,usb4.h,main.c}`; reference `/home/batman/asm2464pd-firmware/handmade/USB4_RE.md`.

Confidence tags carried from the source reports: SB init / SB-router / tunnel-link / adapter-events / connect-e302 = **high**; cm_routerop / tunnel_bringup = **medium**.

## 2. The sideband-assert keystone (verbatim → handmade `sb.h`)

This is the make-or-break for E302. It is the bank1 tail of `usb4_connect_u4` reached at `0xa51b/0xa51e`. In the flat image **every SB access is**: `DPX=1; XDATA_REG8V(0x2800+off) = v; DPX=0` (RMW: read with DPX=1, modify, write with DPX=1, then `DPX=0`). This is the proven equivalent of the stock R3=2/R2=0x28/R1=off paged accessor (`0x0ac1`/`0x0adc` set `DPX=R3-1=1`). handmade already controls DPX for PHY regs, so the pattern is available. Define `SB_REG8(off)` = `XDATA_REG8V(0x2800+off)` wrapped in `DPX=1 … DPX=0`.

**Caller precondition (already partly in `usb4.h` head — keep, then append the tail):**
```
if (0x07BA != 0) {            // Enter_USB-accepted gate
  0x09FA = 0x09F9 & 0x03;
  if (0x09F4 == 3) { if (0x07BE==0){0x09FA=2;0x09FB=1;} else {0x09FA=1;0x09FB=2;} }
  if (0x09FA & 0x02) {
    E716 = E716 & 0xFC; E716 = (E716 & 0xFC) | 0x03;
    DPX=1; XDATA(0x28D8)=2; DPX=0;        // SB[0xd8]=2
  }
  // ... bank1 path-state tail a48c..a516 (see §3 SB-init phase for the helper RMWs) ...
  XDATA(0x07FF) = 0;
  sb_lane_flip_init();   // b230 — run FIRST
  sb_block_init();       // bb37 — run SECOND
}
```

### `sb_lane_flip_init` (b230) — FIRST
```
uart_puts("[flp="); flip = REG8(0xC6DB) & 0x01; uart_puthex(flip); uart_puts("]");

// page-1 0x010100 (NOT SB block): DPX=1
P1[0x0100] &= ~0x10; P1[0x0100] &= ~0x40; P1[0x0100] &= ~0x80;   // clr bits 4,6,7

if (0x07BA!=0 || 0x07B9!=0)  P1[0x0100] &= ~0x01;   // connect: clr bit0
else                         P1[0x0100] |=  0x01;

// orientation-dependent lane map (SB block, DPX=1):
if (flip) {            // C6DB.0 == 1
    SB[0x02] &= ~0x03;
    SB[0x01] &= ~0x03;
} else {               // straight
    SB[0x01] |= 0x01; SB[0x01] |= 0x02;     // lane-map bits0,1
    SB[0x02] |= 0x02;                        // bit1
}                       // ⚠ see Risk R1: exact straight-vs-flip map is host/orientation-interactive

if (0x07BA!=0 || 0x07B9!=0) {
    SB[0x01] = (SB[0x01] & 0xEF) | 0x10;     // clr b5/b6 path -> set b4
    SB[0x01] = (SB[0x01] & 0x7F) | 0x80;     // set b7
    E7FC &= ~0x03;                            // connect pending -> clear bond gate
} else {
    SB[0x01] &= ~0x70; SB[0x01] &= 0x7F;     // clr bits4,5,6,7
    E7FC |= 0x03;                             // no connect -> set bond gate
}

SB[0xd1] = (SB[0xd1] & 0xEF) | 0x10;          // b4=1
SB[0x49] = 0xA0;
XDATA(0x06EC) = 0;
```

### `sb_block_init` (bb37) — SECOND
```
uart_puts("[SB Init]");

// e0d9 PHY descriptor seed (DPX=0 plain XDATA):
C20E=0x3E; C20F=0x08; C210=0x08; C211=0x2E; C212=0x3E;
C214=0x00; C215=0x20; C216=0x00; C217=0x3F;

// page-1 0x010100 head (DPX=1): net &= ~0xD1 (clr bits 0,4,6,7)
P1[0x0100] &= ~0x10; P1[0x0100] &= ~0x40; P1[0x0100] &= ~0x80; P1[0x0100] &= ~0x01;

// --- SB block writes (DPX=1) ---
SB[0x2c]=0x01; SB[0x2c]=0x02;          // net SB[0x2c]=2
SB[0x26]=0x02;
SB[0x66]=0x01;                          // transient (overridden below)
SB[0x2d] &= ~0x01; SB[0x2d] = (SB[0x2d] & 0xFD) | 0x02;   // net b0=0, b1=1
SB[0x29] &= ~0x08;
SB[0x2b] &= ~0x08;
SB[0xc8] &= ~0xF0;                       // clr bits 4,5,6,7
SB[0x27] &= ~0x02;
SB[0x67] &= ~0x81;                       // clr bits 0,7
SB[0x81]=0x08;
SB[0x83]=0x08;
SB[0x82] &= ~0x08;
SB[0x84] &= ~0x08;
SB[0x9e]=0x01; SB[0x9e]=0x02;            // transient (overridden below)
SB[0x66]=0x04; SB[0x66]=0x20;            // FINAL SB[0x66]=0x20
SB[0x9f] &= ~0x03;
SB[0x67] &= ~0x24;                        // clr bits 2,5
SB[0x9e]=0x10; SB[0x9e]=0x20;            // FINAL SB[0x9e]=0x20
SB[0x9f] &= ~0x30;
XDATA(0x06EC) = 0;

// b7a4 ROM descriptor loader (DATA — copy byte-exact, NOT computable):
//   CODE 0x213d[0x64] -> XDATA 0x0800..0x0863 (router/DROM identity: VID 0x174C, PID 0x2464, 'APP EM  ')
//   CODE 0x21d4[0x10] = {0B,0B,0B,0B,0B,0B,0C,0C,0C,0C,0C,07,07,07,07,07} -> XDATA 0x07xx
//   XDATA(0x0804)=XDATA(0x0A57); XDATA(0x0805)=XDATA(0x0A58);
//   if (!(0x09F9 & 0x80)) XDATA(0x081B) &= ~0x02;
//   if (XDATA(0x09F5))    XDATA(0x081A) = (XDATA(0x081A) & 0xDF) | 0x20;

SB[0x01] = (SB[0x01] & 0xBF) | 0x40;     // set bit6
SB[0x01] = (SB[0x01] & 0x7F) | 0x80;     // set bit7   (net bits6,7 set)
SB[0xc4] &= ~0x02;
SB[0x27] &= ~0x14;                        // clr bits 2,4

// --- PHY bank0 RMW (DPX=0) ---
C233 &= ~0x08;
C2C4 = (C2C4 & 0xBF) | 0x40;
C2DC &= 0xC0;
C344 = (C344 & 0xBF) | 0x40;
C35C &= 0xC0;

// e34b PHY lane cfg:
XDATA(0x0AB3)=0; XDATA(0x0AB4)=3; XDATA(0x0AB5)=3; XDATA(0x0AB6)=0;
C2CB &= ~0x04; C34B &= ~0x04; C208 &= ~0x40;
SB[0x1d] &= ~0x02;     // (DPX=1)
```

**Non-SB registers touched in the keystone (so they must exist as plain bank0 XDATA writes):** E716, CA81, CA06 (head), E7FC, C6DB(read), C20E-C217, C233/C2C4/C2DC/C344/C35C, C2CB/C34B/C208, page-1 `0x010100`, and the `0x0800/0x07xx/0x081A/0x081B/0x0AB3-6/0x06EC/0x07FF` XDATA staging.

**Conflict flag:** the `connect_e302` summary lists a shorter SB-offset set (`0x15,0x26,0x27,0x29,0x2B,0x2D,0x66,0x67,0x81,0x83,0x84,0x9E,0xC9`) and `C2DC&=~0x3F`; the **`sideband` report (high-conf, full RMW decode) is authoritative** and gives the fuller set above with `C2DC &= 0xC0`. Use the `sideband` decode. The `0x15`/`0xC9` writes appear only in the shorter summary and are **not** in the detailed decode — do not add them to init (they are W1C'd in the router handler, §3, not seeded here).

## 3. Per-phase implementation spec

### Phase SB-INIT (the keystone, §2) — driver: synchronous tail of `usb4_connect_u4` (no interrupt)
- **Ops:** §2 verbatim. Also reproduce the intermediate bank1 path-state RMWs from `connect_e302` `a48c..a516` that run *before* b230 when `(0x09FA & 0x81)!=0` (the tunnel route): `P1[0x0000] |= 0x02`; on tunnel route `CA06 &= ~0x10`, `P1[0x0000] &= ~0x04`, `d436` width(0xF) (B434 ramp x4 / B436), if `0x0AF1.4`: `E710=(E710&0xE0)|0x1F`, `CC30 &= ~0x01`; `ee82` `B430 |= 0x01`; `0x924C=(0x924C&0xF7)|0x08`; `P1[0x0000] |= 0x04`. These are gated on `0x0AF1` bits and `0x09FA&0x81` — see Risk R3 (0x0AF1 producer un-traced).
- **Pass:** UART prints `[flp=NN][SB Init]`. Then within ~ms the **host raises C80A.5 and E302 climbs** — the real success signal.

### Phase SB-ROUTER — driver: **INT1 C80A.5** (`a066`)
Pure reactive W1C-ack + forward; **never invoke speculatively** (it only acks bits HW set). Replace the `usb4_int_seen|=0x01` no-op in `usb4.h`.
```
idx=0;
for (idx=0; idx<4; idx++) {
  bm = SB[0xC9];
  if ((bm & (1<<(4+idx))) && XDATA(0x06F1)==idx) {
      sb_channel_connect_service();          // c3b2 (below)
      SB[0xC9] = (1<<idx); SB[0xC9] = (1<<(idx+4));   // W1C both halves
      XDATA(0x06F1) = (XDATA(0x06F1)+1) & 3;
      if (P1[0x0109] & 1) sb_lane_bond_complete_tunnel_up();  // e52d -> 0x3578 downstream PCIe
  }
}
sb_transport_substate_poll();                // d4cd: poll SB[0x28/0x2A/0x81/0x83].3
cs = SB[0x2D];
if (cs & 0x01){ uart_puts("[===SB Con===]"); SB[0x66] &= ~0x02; /*dea1*/ }
else if (cs & 0x02){ SB[0x2D]=0x02; uart_puts("[===SB Dis===]"); SB[0x9E] &= ~0x01; /*97fc/da9f*/ }
if (SB[0x66] & 0x01){ SB[0x66]=0x01; uart_puts("[Lane Bonded]"); /*eed6*/ XDATA(0x074E)=0;XDATA(0x074F)=0; }
if (SB[0x26] & 0x02){ /*a5d8*/ SB[0x26]=0x02; }
// L0 CL0 (gated SB[0x9E].0): SB[0x9E]=0x01; "[L0:CL0 ]"; n=SB[0xA0]&0x0F; CL0 if n==2
// L1 CL0 (gated SB[0x9E].1): SB[0x9E]=0x02; "[L1:CL0 ]"; n=SB[0xA1]&0x0F; CL0 if n==2
// SB[0x66] sub-events bits2/5/3/6 -> [L0:Abr2]/[L1:Abr2]/[L0:Bnd Fail]/[L1:Bnd Fail], each W1C
// SB[0x26] bits2/4 -> [L0:Disable]/[L1:Disable], each W1C (+SB[0x15] arm, SB[0x5A]=0x40 on L1)
// SB[0x9E] bits4/5 -> [L0:Training]/[L1:Training], each W1C
status = SB[0xF6];   // tail latch read
```
`sb_channel_connect_service` (c3b2): select pair by `0x06F1` (p0→SB[0x20]/[0x22], p1→[0x21]/[0x23], p2→[0xA4]/[0xA6], p3→[0xA5]/[0xA7]); `0x4E=SB[lo]; 0x4F=SB[hi]; if (~0x4F)!=0x4E print err,return;` then dispatch `0x4E&0x0F`: **1/3 → `XDATA(0x0766)=1`** (route-up); 2 → link-reset (`SB[0x50]=0x40; SB[0x15]|=0x83; da9f`); 6 → special; default → `SB[0x5A]&0x40` read + zero 0x074E/F.
- **Pass:** UART `[===SB Con===]` then `[Lane Bonded]` / `[L0:CL0 ][L1:CL0 ]`; `0x0766` becomes 1.

### Phase CM ROUTER-OP — driver: **INT1 EC06.0** (`c0a5`, conf medium)
Extend the existing `EC04=1` ack in `usb4.h` into the full FSM. Requires `0x0B02-0x0B1F` zero-init at boot.
```
if (PR(EC06)&1) {
  PR(EC04)=1;                                        // ack (already present)
  if (0x0AF1 & 0x20){ E7E3 &= ~0x40; E7E3 &= ~0x80; }
  if (EA90 != 0x5A) return;                          // host doorbell gate
  switch (XDATA(0x0B02)) {                            // FSM state
   case 0: gen=EA80; XDATA(0x0B03)=gen;
           // movc dispatch on gen 0xE0..0xE8; key op = 0xE2 (config r/w):
           //   read EA81 (0x50=cfg-read / 0x51=cfg-write); 0x0004 = EA81&1 (dir);
           //   copy EA82.. (4 bytes) -> 0x0B04 (cfg addr); 0x0B0A = length/limit;
           //   read -> d945 (status 0x80 err / len; C805=(C805&0xF9)|0x02 trigger;
           //            resp hdr 0x0AAD/0x0AB1=0/0x0AB2=status; payload via 0x04c1);
           //   write -> cf5d (C805 trigger; C8B0=0xEA,C8B1=0; C8B2/C8B3=0x7000+0x0B08:09; poll C8B8.0);
           //   if more: 0x0B02 = 1(read)/2(write) continuation;
           break;
   case 1: /* read continuation -> d945 */ break;
   case 2: /* write continuation -> cf5d */ break;
  }
  EA90 = 0xA5;                                        // response-ready handshake
}
```
Also wire `[ConnRout]` (`a820`): `if (0x0777==0x0C && 0x07B9 && (0x0778&0x7F)==2){ confirm 0x0776; uart_puts("[ConnRout]"); 0x0718=0x04; }` — this is the fixed load-bearing route-enable.
- **Pass:** `EA90` cycles 0x5A→0xA5; `[ConnRout]`; `0x0718==0x04`; the host fills `0x0A52/53/54` / `0x0AEC/AED` (verify via XDATA dump). **Do not invoke opcode 0xE8 (`e4a6`) speculatively** — it asserts CC31 HW-reset + `sjmp $`.

### Phase TUNNEL-LINK ack — driver: **INT1 C80A.0-3** (`e911`)
Already correct in `usb4.h` (gate C80A.0, W1C E763 bit2/bit3). Add the markers:
```
if (PR(C80A)&0x01) {
  e763=PR(E763);
  if (e763&0x04){ PR(E763)=0x04; uart_puts("[PcieTunnel-PcieLinkUp]"); }
```

- **Pass:** `[PcieTunnel-PcieLinkUp]` on UART.

### Phase TUNNEL BRING-UP + DOWNSTREAM PCIe — driver: route/CM state + `0x05B4==0x10` (conf medium)
Boot pre-stage (`d996`, run once at boot before USB4): `e57d` E764 reset pulse (`&=~2,~1,~8,(&~4)|4`); `B432=(B432&0xF8)|0x07`; `B404=(B404&0xF0)|0x01`; `d436` width. ## 4. The "E302 trains" question — resolved

**What makes `(E302>>4)&3 → 3`:** The firmware **never writes E302** (all sites are reads: a6ef/b394/be8b/bf04). E302 is set by the upstream USB4 PHY/SERDES **after the device asserts the sideband (§2) and the host completes USB4 entry in response to the PD Enter_USB ACCEPT**. So the single thing that "trains E302" is **running `b230 + sb_block_init` to completion** — the SB-block bits (SB[0x81]=0x08, SB[0x01].6/.7, SB[0x66]=0x20, SB[0x9e]=0x20, the lane map, E7FC bond gate) are exactly what the host's connection manager polls to begin lane training. Today handmade stops at the RE boundary and emits **no** SB writes, so the host has nothing to train against → E302 stays 0. `(E302>>4)&3>=2` is **not** a precondition to *run* `sb_block_init`; it is the *consequence*.

**Must the forced `0x09F9=1` change? YES — and this is a real bug, but not the one its comment implies.** `pd.h:213` does `PR(0x09F9) = 0x01`. The keystone resolution (`connect_e302`, high conf): `0x09F9` bit7 is the VDM-ACK enable. With `0x09F9=0x01`, **bit7 is clear**, which makes Discover_Identity / Discover_SVIDs / Discover_Modes / EnterMode all **NAK** — and on the `&3` route latch, `0x09FA=0x09F9&3=1` mis-selects the route. The faithful runtime value is **`0x87`** (bit7 set so VDM ACK gates pass; bits2:0 = mode; with 0x87 → `0x09FA=3`, so `(0x09FA&0x81)!=0` selects the tunnel route and `0x09FA.1` fires `SB[0xd8]=2`+E716 reflip). **Note on the gate:** the INT1 demux gate `(0x09F9 & 0x83)` is satisfied by both 0x01 and 0x87, so the handlers were already reachable — the bug is purely the VDM-NAK / wrong-route from bit7=0 and bits1:0=01. **Fix: `PR(0x09F9) = 0x87;`** Forcing `0x09F9=1` does **not** wrongly trigger the 92E1 mode-entry latch (that latch in `d78a` is gated on bit6, clear in both 0x01 and 0x87), so the 92E1 concern is a non-issue — the only required change is the value 0x01→0x87. (Long-term: replace the force with the real boot mode-decision `0xB1CB`→`usb4_cap_apply_09f9 @0x8D77`, which produces 0x87/0x85/0xC1/0x06/0x04 from negotiated mode.)

## 5. Implementation order with HW-verifiable milestones

| Milestone | Concrete handmade change | Marker / register to check |
|-----------|--------------------------|----------------------------|
| **M0 (prereq)** | `pd.h:213`: `PR(0x09F9)=0x01` → **`0x87`**. Zero-init `0x0B02-0x0B1F` (and `0x06F1=0`) at boot. Add `SB_REG8(off)` page-1 accessor + `sb.h`. | VDM ACKs resume on CY4500 (no NAK on Discover_Identity); `0x09FA==3` after Connect_U4 |
| **M1 — E302 trains** | Add `sb_lane_flip_init` (b230) + `sb_block_init` (bb37) verbatim (§2) and call them as the `usb4_connect_u4` tail (after the route latch). Transcribe the two ROM tables + PHY descriptor bytes. | UART `[flp=NN][SB Init]`, then **`(E302>>4)&3` climbs 0→2/3** (super-loop already prints `[U` E302). **This is the keystone gate.** |
| **M2 — SB connect** | Replace `usb4.h` C80A.5 no-op with `sb_router_event_handler` (a066, §3) incl. `sb_channel_connect_service` (c3b2). | UART `[===SB Con===]` then `[Lane Bonded]` / `[L0:CL0 ][L1:CL0 ]`; `0x0766==1`; C80A.5 stops re-firing (W1C works) |
| **M3 — tunnel link** | Wire CM router-op FSM (c0a5, §3) on EC06.0; `[ConnRout]` `0x0718=0x04`; tunnel adapter cfg/enable (`c8db`/`cd6c`/`ee82`); downstream `9037`/`a840`/`cdc6`/`3578`; add E763 markers. | UART `[ConnRout]`, `[PcieTunnel-PcieLinkUp]`, `[*** PCIE Gen N x M]`; `(B432&7)==7 && (E765&2)`; `E763` W1C clean |

## 6. Risks / open questions (host-interactive or data-dependent — cannot be pure register replay)

- **R1 — SB lane-map orientation (M1).** `b230`'s final `SB[0x01]/SB[0x02]` bits differ by `C6DB.0` (flip) and the connect flags. The bit ops are decoded but the *intended* per-orientation lane assignment is host-interactive. **Verify:** the `[flp=N]` print reveals the runtime orientation; capture page-1 `0x01xx` on a real flip vs straight plug; if the host rejects, compare against a stock SB-init MMIO trace.
- **R2 — ROM descriptor tables (M1).** `CODE 0x213d[0x64]` (router DROM: VID 0x174C/PID 0x2464/'APP EM ') and `0x21d4[0x10]` are **data the host CM reads back**; must be copied byte-exact. **Verify:** they live in `fw_tinygrad.bin` (ghidra offset == file offset); dump them and embed verbatim; if the host rejects the router, diff against a working capture.
- **R3 — `0x0AF1` gate bits + `0x09F4` DP-alt (M1).** Bits 0/4/5 of `0x0AF1` select which connect_u4 sub-blocks run; producer is in the earlier router/cable-mode path, not traced. **Verify:** read `0x0AF1`/`0x09F4` on HW with a plain USB4-C cable to the AMD host; the expected path is `(0x09FA&0x81)!=0` tunnel route.
- **R4 — All SB-router event bits are HW-set (M2).** `SB[0xC9]/[0x2D]/[0x66]/[0x9E]/[0x26]` and the `SB[0xA0]/[0xA1]` CL0 nibbles are set by SB HW from host sideband traffic — none are fixed writes; the handler only reads+W1C. **Verify:** CY4500 / UART markers; the handler must never be invoked speculatively. Side flags `0x0819/0x09F2/0x09F3/0x0B1C` and the `0x05a7` per-lane notify are gates whose producers weren't traced — copy conditionals verbatim.
- **R5 — CM mailbox wire content (M3, conf medium).** Host CM writes EA80/EA81/EA82../EA90; the exact route-string vs adapter# vs config byte-ordering, the full opcode map (only 0xE2 config and 0xE8 reset firmly identified), the config-space READ payload backing (`0x04c1` — fixed CPU table vs latched B2xx/B4xx?), and the EA90 handshake/chunking (7-byte cap) are **not** statically provable. **Verify:** MMIO trace of EA80-EA85/EA90 + `0x0B04` during a live CM transaction; XDATA dump of `0x0A52/53/54`/`0x0AEC/AED` after.
- **R6 — Tunnel vs direct-PCIe integration (M4).** Open whether the AMD GPU in `DEV=USB+AMD` is reached via this CM/EC06 tunnel path (steps 5-9) or via handmade's existing direct `pcie_*.h` boot path (trains downstream PHY at boot, no tunnel). The `0x05B4==0x10` trigger writer was not found in bank0 (likely a bank1 LTSSM poll). `B455.1`/`B432&7`/`E765.2` are GPU/cable-timing-dependent, not fixed delays. **Verify:** stock MMIO trace of whether the GPU appears via EC06/CM (B410/B401/B430 path) or via the direct B480/E764 path; watchpoint `0x05B4`.
- **R7 — Page-1 alias for adapter-event regs (M3, minor).** `0x1407/0x1603/0x1203/0x124e/0x128f` are derived as page-1 (DPX=1) from R3=2 routing; `registers.h` currently treats them as plain xdata. **Verify:** one-shot HW read at both DPX pages to confirm the live event alias.
- **R8 — `e4a6` (opcode 0xE8) CPU-reset hazard (M3).** Contains `CC31|=1` (HW reset) + unconditional `sjmp $`. Whether the host drives this in the happy GPU path or only on teardown is unresolved — **do not invoke speculatively**; treat as CPU-resetting.

**Conflict ledger:** (a) SB offset set — `sideband` (high) is authoritative over `connect_e302` summary (§2); use `C2DC &= 0xC0`, final `SB[0x66]=0x20`, `SB[0x9e]=0x20`; do **not** add `SB[0x15]`/`SB[0xC9]` to init. (b) `registers.h` mislabels: `E763`=tunnel link-event (not RXPLL trigger), `B432`=lane status (not power-ctrl), `CC3F`=Type-C SBU (not LTSSM ctrl), `0x1407/0x1603`=page-1 — fix names when adding `sb.h`/`registers_usb4.h`. (c) The `usb4.h` HONEST-RE-BOUNDARY comment ("part B un-RE-able, no SB writes") is now **superseded** by the high-conf `sideband` decode — part B is recoverable and is the keystone; update that comment when implementing M1.
